Subject: Reserved capacity ask: sensitivity to GPU cost moves

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’ve got internal momentum to move ahead with a committed capacity arrangement, but procurement wants a sensitivity view tied to GPU price moves and a clear approval path for any incremental discounts. High level asks:

- A 3-option commit (6m / 12m / 24m) with "unit token cost" and per-token delta under three GPU cost scenarios (base / -20% / +15%).
- Minimum capacity guarantee and recommended burst strategy (how to preserve latency while saving cost).
- What discount thresholds require FT approvals vs exec sign-off and how long a pricing window you can hold.
- A timeline: internal approvals + DocuSign for a Dec closing.

Can you send a short pack and the approval path? We want to review with procurement on Dec 2.

Cheers,
Sana Malik
VP of Engineering, Acme Cloud

  * Option A: 6-month commit (medium discount) — low risk, flexible upgrade path

Jonas / team —

Quick finance guidance based on the draft:

- Discount thresholds (by policy):
  * <= 12% off list for committed capacity: Sales director approval (auto-approvable in portal)
  * 12% < discount <= 25%: FP&A + Finance Manager approval; requires escalation ticket and usage floor in contract (min monthly tokens).
  * > 25%: VP Finance sign-off + legal review of MFN clause.

- For 24-month deep commits we need to model GPU-cost step-downs explicitly and include a CPI-style passthrough if HW market moves >+20% to protect margin. Without a passthrough, max allowable discount today is 28% for 24m (with prepay).
- I need the scenario-level gross margin per month (sheet tab: MARGIN_MODEL) and an estimated cashflow schedule (prepay vs monthly invoice).

Related: procurement will want a short SLA on latency/uptime tied to capacity; we should avoid hard latency SLOs that extend beyond our Dedicated SLA unless we add canary buffer in the first 30 days.

I’m OK to greenlight up to 18% on a 12m if we get a 6-month early termination penalty and usage floors. Above that, loop Marissa + VP.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity ask: sensitivity to GPU cost moves

Adding technical sizing notes (attached runbook). High-level: 

- Recommended dedicated pool sizing for Option B (12m): start with 8x A800-equivalent GPUs with a 20% headroom buffer for peak windows. That maps to expected 95th pct latency under current model mix for their projected Q1 load.
- Option C (24m, deep commit): recommend mixing A800 + 2x A100 res slots for burst-only heavy batches; this preserves cost while enabling occasional long-generation workloads.
- Canary / rollout: provision an isolated canary shard (1 GPU) + staggered traffic ramp over 10 days. KV-cache warmup will reduce token bill during ramp but counts against prefunded commit — note that for financial modeling.
- Autoscaling: recommend 2-tier autoscale: fast-burst (pre-allocated warm slots) + cold-burst (hosted fallback). Include fallback to hosted smaller models for risk-mitigation if GPU spot pricing spikes or capacity saturation.

Attachments: gpu_runbook.pdf

Caveat: if Acme requires hard latency SLOs with penalties, we should limit exposure and increase buffer (adds ~12–15% to committed cost).

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Three offer options (see attached SUMMARY in the workbook):
  1) 6 months — modest discount, flexible upgrade; minimal signoff required
  2) 12 months — best balance; we can approve up to 18% discount with Finance conditions (usage floors / 6m early termination)
  3) 24 months — deepest saving (up to 28% with prepay) but requires VP-level signoff and a CPI-style passthrough for >+20% GPU cost swings

- Technical controls: recommended dedicated pool sizes (12m plan: 8x A800 equiv + 20% buffer), canary shard for rollout, and hosted-fallback for extreme price moves. See attached runbook for operational details.
- Timeline: if Procurement confirms preference by Dec 2, we will lock pricing for a 14-day hold and target DocuSign execution by Dec 15.

Attachments: acme_reserved_scenarios.xlsx, gpu_runbook.pdf, MPA-draft-acme.docx
